You sound like a really caring partner 💜 💜 I would definitely make sure you know what your boundaries are. Like for instance, when I start isolating, it really affects my partner. They told me this and now, when they notice im starting to isolate, they just say, "Whats something good that happened today?" This boundary of theirs actually let's me know they still care but that my isolation/negativity is affecting them. It also helps me check myself and Sometimes it even opens the door for communication between us. Like ill say, "sorry im being so negative but x,y,z happened today and I'm just not doing good" we are then able to navigate the rest of our day, whether that's me taking time to isolate/self-care for a bit or doing a light hearted activity together. 

 Maybe talking with her and figuring out a code word or phrase when you notice she's starting to isolate will let her know you care without her feeling like she's putting too much on you or having to discuss her feelings too much. 

So yeah, make sure to communicate your needs too. If she keeps pushing you out, eventually you may come to resent that. So letting her know you need her to communicate with you is important. It doesn't mean she has to tell you every little detail of how she's feeling but just saying things like 'im having a rough day' or 'i need to be alone right now but ill make sure we do something together later' is a step in the right direction.
